rows: A bee can just resolve stripes at about a quarter of a cycle for each degree of view. A person manages 30 or more, so a bee's picture is more than a hundred times coarser than yours.
The two compound eyes together cover about 312 degrees at the horizon, with the field reaching nearly all round. Only a small blind wedge of about 48 degrees remains behind the head.

Bees have three kinds of colour receptor, tuned to ultraviolet, blue and green light, with peaks near 344, 436 and 540 nanometres. They can see ultraviolet but not far red, so the view shifts colours toward shorter wavelengths.
bee.jsonl:German Aerospace Center (DLR) and Bee Sensory and Behavioural Ecology Lab 2026
A honeybee's eye can follow flicker up to about 200 times a second in bright light, while a person stops at about 60. In this view the world moves at a pace a bee could follow and you cannot.

Phone cameras record almost no ultraviolet, so the app reads part of the blue as ultraviolet and draws it as a tint. The strength of that tint, the mapping of camera colours onto the bee's receptors, and the placement and soft edge of the blind wedge are all the app's choices.
